Postuler Date limite de candidature : jeudi 17 décembre 2026 23:59

Description du Poste

Les Missions

Des candidatures sont sollicitées pour 2 CDD chercheur (H/F) en QCD sur réseau et ses applications à la phénoménologie. Les agents recrutés devront collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe de théorie des particules du CPT sur des projets visant à améliorer notre compréhension de la structure des hadrons. L'objectif principal des postes seraient d'effectuer des simulations QCD sur réseau et d'effectuer l'analyse de données ultérieures nécessaires à l'extraction des distributions de partons (ciblant à la fois les PDFs et les PDFs généralisés). Par ailleurs, les recruté-es seront appelés à participer plus largement aux activités de l'équipe Théorie des Particules, ainsi qu'à celles du CPT.

L'Activité

Les projets impliqueront une variété d'activités. Celles-ci incluent entre autres :

L'exécution de simulations à grande échelle afin de calculer les blocs de construction des fonctions de corrélation nécessaires qui doivent être calculées ;
L' analyse des données pour l'extraction des éléments de la matrice ``clés" ainsi que le post-traitement nécessaire qui conduit aux résultats finaux des distributions du cône de lumière ;
Une collaboration étroite avec nos collaborateurs en France (CEA, Saclay) ainsi qu'à l'étranger (College of William & Mary et JLAB, USA) est également attendue ainsi qu'une participation au partage des résultats avec la communauté scientifique et plus largement, lorsque cela est pertinent.

Votre Profil

Compétences

) Bonne connaissance pratique de la physique théorique hadronique/nucléaire/des particules et de la théorie des champs sur réseau ;
) Indépendance et capacité à collaborer de manière productive ;
) Solides compétences en communication écrite et orale ;
) Solides compétences en programmation (C, C++, Python, bash etc.).

Votre Environnement de Travail

L'activité se déroulera au sein de l'équipe Physique des particules du CPT, dont fait partie le groupe QCD sur réseau. Ce dernier est composé de trois permanents (Antoine Gérardin, Laurent Lellouch, Savvas Zafeiropoulos), de chercheurs en CDD et de trois doctorants. L'équipe élargie de physique des particules compte également comme membres Aoife Bharucha, Jérôme Charles et Marc Knecht.

Ces postes sont financés par la bourse ERC Consolidator récemment octroyée à Savvas Zafeiropoulos. Les travaux de la QCD sur réseau seront menés dans le cadre de la collaboration Hadstruc.

La bourse ERC Consolidator, intitulée HADaSTRaLS – De la structure hadronique 1D à 3D par simulations QCD sur réseau exascale – a été attribuée à Savvas Zafeiropoulos et financera plusieurs postes de CDD chercheur (M/F) et de doctorant (M/F) pour les cinq prochaines années.

Le Centre de Physique Théorique (CPT) est une unité de recherche qui compte une soixantaine de permanents et une quarantaine de doctorants (M/F) et chercheurs (M/F) en CDD effectuant des recherches théoriques dans une grande variété de domaines. Aix-Marseille U. dispose également de fortes unités de recherche en physique expérimentale des particules (CPPM) et en astrophysique, cosmologie et physique des astroparticules (CPPM, LAM).

Contraintes et risques

Utilisation d'ordinateurs, y compris d’écrans.

Pratique et indemnisation du TT

À propos de l’offre

Référence de l’offre UMR7332-CATLEV-066 Section(s) CN / Domaine de recherche Physique théorique : méthodes, modèles et applications

À propos du CNRS

Le CNRS est un acteur majeur de la recherche fondamentale à une échelle mondiale. Le CNRS est le seul organisme français actif dans tous les domaines scientifiques. Sa position unique de multi-spécialiste lui permet d’associer les différentes disciplines pour affronter les défis les plus importants du monde contemporain, en lien avec les acteurs du changement.

jobs.title: Research Assistant EU-wide characterization soil microbiomes
jobs.description:
Your job

Soils are teeming with life. Some soil organisms support plant growth while others use plants as a food source. A notorious example of plant pathogens is root-knot nematodes (RKN) as they have an enormous host range and are widely distributed throughout the subtropical and tropical regions.

Due to global warming, these RKNs are expanding their ranges, and in the framework of a European project named Nem-Emerge we are mapping the current distribution of “tropical” root-knot nematodes. This is not trivial, as they very much look alike.

As a Research Assistant in the European Nem-Emerge project, you will map the current RKN distribution by characterizing samples collected along two major latitudinal transects. In addition, you will also characterize the soil microbial communities that are associated with these nematodes. A combination of long-read DNA sequencing technology and bioinformatics will allow us to map the current distribution and identify microbial antagonists that are associated with these pathogens.

Your work will contribute to a better understanding of range-expanding nematode species and the natural suppressive capacity of the associated soils. Together with researchers across Europe, you will help to generate knowledge that can support more resilient soils and sustainable agriculture.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

You will combine advanced molecular techniques, bioinformatics and scientific interpretation. Your main responsibilities are:

analyzing root-knot nematode communities using long-read DNA sequencing technology;
analyzing associated microbial assemblages using long-read DNA sequencing technology;
bioinformatics-based analyses of nematode and microbial communities;
reporting on results to workpackage leads;
communication with European project partners about results and interpretation thereof;
reporting on results to workpackage leads.

Your team

You will work with Hans Helder and Aska Goverse - the Nem-Emerge project coordinators -, as well as with two PhDs that are currently employed on the project. Together, you will exchange knowledge, interpret findings and contribute to the project's scientific objectives.

You will work here

The full title of the EU Horizon Europe project Nem-Emerge is ‘An integrated set of novel approaches to counter the emergence and proliferation of invasive and virulent soil-borne nematodes’. In this position you will contribute to (a) identifying the current distribution of “tropical” root-knot nematode (RKN) species, as well as (b) mapping the endogenous RKN-suppressive capacity of soils.

Your qualities

You have experience in the DNA-based characterization of (soil) microbiomes, preferably using long-read DNA sequencing technologies, as well as with the associated bioinformatics tools

You Also Possess

qualification: MSc in biology, plant sciences, soil sciences or related;
preferably hands-on experience in (soil) microbiome characterization;
hands-on bioinformatics skills (relevant R-packages);
demonstrable (international) project communication skills.

In our international working environment, there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about minimally B2 level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale).

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our collective labour agreement include:

sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. Depending on your experience, we offer a gross salary of between € 3,537.- and € 4,673.- for a full-time working week of 38 hours, in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (https://www.universiteitenvannederland.nl/en/collective-labour-agreement-of-dutch-universities) (scale 8). Additionally, a contract for 0,8 FTE can be discussed. We offer you a temporary contract for the duration of one year.

If you are an internal employee, your current contract is the starting point. Ask your HR Business Partner about your situation specifically. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy (https://wur.service-now.com/esc?id=kb_article&sysparm_article=KB0012172) sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

Coming from abroad

WUR welcomes applications from international candidates. However, for applicants for this specific position from outside the EU/EFTA zone, immigration restrictions may apply based on Dutch and EU immigration laws. Such candidates may be eligible for an “ orientation year ” in the Netherlands or a visa as a “ knowledge migrant ”.

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. If you come with a partner, we offer a Dual Career group program organized by our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/). This program helps your partner to get familiar with the Dutch culture, labour market and assists your partner to find a job.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/expats-new-international-staff) page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.

Important information

For more information about the position, please contact Hans Helder, Associate Professor Laboratory of Nematology, via phone number: +31 17-483136 or via email: hans.helder@wur.nl (mailto:hans.helder@wur.nl).

Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Dax Teunissen, Corporate Recruiter, via email: vacaturemeldingen.psg@wur.nl (mailto:vacaturemeldingen.psg@wur.nl).

Ready to apply?

Click on the application button next to the vacancy on our website. Only applications submitted through our website will be considered.

You can apply up to and including Monday 21 December 2026
. Internal candidates are preferred to apply before 27 November 2026.

Applications are reviewed regularly. Therefore, the position may be filled before the stated closing date.

Welcome, safe, and valued

Wageningen University & Research (WUR) highly values diversity and inclusion because we believe that different insights lead to innovative solutions. We create a work environment where everyone feels welcome, safe, and appreciated, regardless of background, identity, or experience. Together, we are building a culture where everyone's unique contribution adds to the success of our organization.

We are

The mission of Wageningen University & Research is “To explore the potential of nature to improve the quality of life”. Under the banner Wageningen University & Research, Wageningen University and the specialised research institutes of the Wageningen Research Foundation have joined forces in contributing to finding solutions to important questions in the domain of healthy food and living environment. With its roughly 30 branches, 7,600 employees (6,700 fte) and 13,100 students and over 150,000 participants to WUR’s Life Long Learning, Wageningen University & Research is one of the leading organisations in its domain. The unique Wageningen approach lies in its integrated approach to issues and the collaboration between different disciplines.

jobs.title: Research & Development (R&D) Specialist Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Overview

University Hospital Southampton is delighted to offer a fantastic opportunity to work with us

Job Title: Research & Development (R&D) Specialist Data Analyst

Contract Type: Permanent

Please be advised that this vacancy may close earlier than stated if we receive a large number of applications.

Main duties of the job

This is an exciting opportunity to join our growing Data & AI team within the Research & Development department at University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, as a Senior Research Analyst.

Working within the Southampton Emerging Therapies and Technologies (SETT) Centre, you will combine advanced analytical and data engineering expertise with line management responsibilities, leading a group of analysts and data engineers to deliver high-quality research data projects.

Our team supports clinical and academic research through the extraction, processing and analysis of routinely collected healthcare data, developing innovative tools and infrastructure to expand research capacity and improve patient outcomes.

You will play an important role in supporting research project delivery, ensuring technical quality, and working in the team to improve team processes and capabilities.

The SETT Data & AI team works to drive future transformation in patient care through the streamlined extraction of high quality data at scale, and the application of state of the art analytical techniques to drive research. By developing a data landscape friendly to research, we aim to expand Trust-wide research capacity and improve patient outcomes through helping to shape the future of medicine. This is a creative and rapidly evolving unit within the hospital’s R&D environment, and successful candidates will have the exciting opportunity to help shape its direction and long-term aims.

Working for our organisation

As one of the largest acute teaching Trusts in England, we offer learning and development opportunities to help you achieve the career you aspire to. UHS is rated ‘Good’ by the CQC and in the latest national NHS Staff Survey, we were in the top 10 acute trusts for staff engagement and for staff recommending the hospital as a place to work or receive care.

We support flexible working and will consider requests taking into account the needs of the service. UHS employees are able to access a range of NHS discounts, are entitled to a minimum of 35 days paid holiday (pro rata), and we offer a generous pension scheme.

Southampton is an attractive place to live and work situated on the south coast, with an international airport and direct trains to London. The New Forest National Park and beaches of the Jurassic coast are also right on our doorstep. The city offers living costs 30% lower than London and 17 schools rated outstanding by Ofsted.

We believe that using technology wisely shows strong time management and commitment to innovation. However, personalising your recruitment application to highlight your unique skills and experiences is crucial. Relying too heavily on generic, AI-generated content instead of drawing from your own strengths and accomplishments may lead to your application being rejected if multiple candidates present identical or similar information.

Detailed Job Description And Main Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting the delivery of complex research data analysis projects within the Data & AI team. You will support project development and delivery, maintain high technical standards, and contribute to the ongoing improvement of the team's capabilities and working practices.

The Data & AI team works closely with clinical and academic researchers across University Hospital Southampton and partner organisations, supporting a diverse portfolio of research projects using routinely collected healthcare data. Our work ranges from developing automated data extraction and transformation pipelines to undertaking advanced analytical studies, building innovative research tools and improving the infrastructure that enables research at scale. Through this work, we aim to expand research capacity, support scientific discovery and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

Research project development and delivery: Develop and manage a pipeline of research data projects, guiding enquiries from initial Expression of Interest through feasibility assessment, scoping, resource estimation and prioritisation into active delivery. Support the analytical delivery of allocated projects, monitoring progress, and working closely with researchers and research delivery teams to ensure projects meet their scientific and technical requirements.
Technical and analytical leadership: Undertake complex analyses of routinely collected NHS healthcare data, alongside the design and development of robust, reproducible data extraction, transformation and processing pipelines across clinical information systems. Provide technical oversight, including code review, testing, validation and documentation, while supporting the adoption of consistent technical standards and high-quality development practices.
Infrastructure, governance and service development: Contribute to the design and improvement of research data infrastructure, analytical tooling, development environments and automation capabilities to enable efficient and scalable study delivery. Help develop and embed team processes, policies and technical standards through knowledge-sharing, ensuring appropriate information governance and research compliance.

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for a motivated and experienced analyst with an interest in advancing healthcare research.

The following skills and experience would position you well for this role:

Advanced analytical and engineering expertise: Educated to degree level in a numerate or scientific discipline, alongside substantial professional experience in data analysis or data engineering with strong SQL and Python skills, experience working with complex datasets, and a sound understanding of reproducible data processing, software development and quality assurance.
Project delivery and client-facing experience: Demonstrable experience of coordinating and delivering complex analytical or engineering projects in a client-facing environment, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders, understand requirements, assess feasibility, agree deliverables, manage expectations and communicate progress, supported by strong interpersonal, communication and relationship-management skills.
Technical judgement and continuous improvement: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, experience of handling sensitive information, an understanding of data protection and quality assurance requirements, and the ability to independently resolve technical challenges, improve working practices and support colleagues through knowledge-sharing and mentoring.

Person specification

Qualifications

Essential criteria

Educated to degree level or able to demonstrate equivalent level of knowledge/research experience relevant to the role.

Knowledge and Experience

Essential criteria

Significant experience of working with SQL to directly interrogate organisational data
Experienced use of Python programming in a working environment for engineering, data science or research
Experience of working with complex data across multiple disparate databases and multi-user environments, being able to demonstrate knowledge of these databases/ software.
Experience of medical research methodology and statutory clinical trial regulations, GCP and research governance requirements.
Experience of clinical trials in the NHS or the commercial health research sector.
Evidence of continuing professional development.
Evidence of ongoing/current Good Clinical Practice Training (GCP)
Thorough understanding of the systems and processes which are used to support the delivery of high quality clinical care in a research environment.
An understanding of R&D issues in the NHS.
Knowledge of research governance and quality assurance systems to ensure safe systems for patients.
Experience of previous training in monitoring of clinical research studies.
Knowledge of data governance requirements including GDPR

Desirable criteria

Commercial research experience.
Previous experience in using IRAS for R&D applications
Experience of working with additional programming languages
Experience of applying machine learning/LLMs within data engineering pipelines
Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, or CI/CD development
Ability to work in multi-disciplinary teams, working with technical and non-technical persons
Experience of working collaboratively with version control tools such as Git

for this vacancy

We have an exciting opportunity for a band 2 Biomedical Support Worker to work in our Blood Transfusion Laboratory at UHS.

We are looking for a motivated individual to join our BSW team to support our Blood Transfusion Laboratory service. We offer full training and development into the role and opportunities for further development.

Working for our organisation

University Hospital Southampton is one of England's largest acute teaching Trusts, offering a wide range of learning and development opportunities to support your career aspirations.

Located on the south coast with an international airport and direct rail links to London, Southampton offers an ideal setting to live and work, with the New Forest, South Downs and Jurassic Coast.

We believe that using technology wisely shows strong time management and commitment to innovation. However, personalizing your recruitment application to highlight your unique skills and experiences is crucial. Relying too heavily on generic, AI-generated content instead of drawing from your own strengths and accomplishments may lead to your application being rejected if multiple candidates present identical or similar information.

At UHS we’re committed to providing a flexible working environment where possible. Whether you are balancing family, study, or your wellbeing with your career, we want to support you so you can help our patients.

At UHS, we proudly champion individuality, recognizing that outstanding care is only possible with a diverse, inclusive team. We’re committed to creating an anti-racist, anti-discriminatory environment where everyone feels valued, safe, and empowered to make a meaningful impact in our communities. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences to join us in building a healthcare community where everyone can belong, thrive, and contribute.

In this role, your key responsibilities will include:

To receive blood components and products into the laboratory ensuring the cold chain has

Description du Poste

Les Missions

Des candidatures sont sollicitées pour 2 CDD chercheur (H/F) en QCD sur réseau et ses applications à la phénoménologie. Les agents recrutés devront collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe de théorie des particules du CPT sur des projets visant à améliorer notre compréhension de la structure des hadrons. L'objectif principal des postes seraient d'effectuer des simulations QCD sur réseau et d'effectuer l'analyse de données ultérieures nécessaires à l'extraction des distributions de partons (ciblant à la fois les PDFs et les PDFs généralisés). Par ailleurs, les recruté-es seront appelés à participer plus largement aux activités de l'équipe Théorie des Particules, ainsi qu'à celles du CPT.

L'Activité

Les projets impliqueront une variété d'activités. Celles-ci incluent entre autres :

L'exécution de simulations à grande échelle afin de calculer les blocs de construction des fonctions de corrélation nécessaires qui doivent être calculées ;
L' analyse des données pour l'extraction des éléments de la matrice ``clés" ainsi que le post-traitement nécessaire qui conduit aux résultats finaux des distributions du cône de lumière ;
Une collaboration étroite avec nos collaborateurs en France (CEA, Saclay) ainsi qu'à l'étranger (College of William & Mary et JLAB, USA) est également attendue ainsi qu'une participation au partage des résultats avec la communauté scientifique et plus largement, lorsque cela est pertinent.

Compétences

) Bonne connaissance pratique de la physique théorique hadronique/nucléaire/des particules et de la théorie des champs sur réseau ;
) Indépendance et capacité à collaborer de manière productive ;
) Solides compétences en communication écrite et orale ;
) Solides compétences en programmation (C, C++, Python, bash etc.).

Votre Environnement de Travail

L'activité se déroulera au sein de l'équipe Physique des particules du CPT, dont fait partie le groupe QCD sur réseau. Ce dernier est composé de trois permanents (Antoine Gérardin, Laurent Lellouch, Savvas Zafeiropoulos), de chercheurs en CDD et de trois doctorants. L'équipe élargie de physique des particules compte également comme membres Aoife Bharucha, Jérôme Charles et Marc Knecht.

Ces postes sont financés par la bourse ERC Consolidator récemment octroyée à Savvas Zafeiropoulos. Les travaux de la QCD sur réseau seront menés dans le cadre de la collaboration Hadstruc.

La bourse ERC Consolidator, intitulée HADaSTRaLS – De la structure hadronique 1D à 3D par simulations QCD sur réseau exascale – a été attribuée à Savvas Zafeiropoulos et financera plusieurs postes de CDD chercheur (M/F) et de doctorant (M/F) pour les cinq prochaines années.

Le Centre de Physique Théorique (CPT) est une unité de recherche qui compte une soixantaine de permanents et une quarantaine de doctorants (M/F) et chercheurs (M/F) en CDD effectuant des recherches théoriques dans une grande variété de domaines. Aix-Marseille U. dispose également de fortes unités de recherche en physique expérimentale des particules (CPPM) et en astrophysique, cosmologie et physique des astroparticules (CPPM, LAM).

new_jobs.title: Research Assistant EU-wide characterization soil microbiomes
new_jobs.description:
Your job

Soils are teeming with life. Some soil organisms support plant growth while others use plants as a food source. A notorious example of plant pathogens is root-knot nematodes (RKN) as they have an enormous host range and are widely distributed throughout the subtropical and tropical regions.

Due to global warming, these RKNs are expanding their ranges, and in the framework of a European project named Nem-Emerge we are mapping the current distribution of “tropical” root-knot nematodes. This is not trivial, as they very much look alike.

As a Research Assistant in the European Nem-Emerge project, you will map the current RKN distribution by characterizing samples collected along two major latitudinal transects. In addition, you will also characterize the soil microbial communities that are associated with these nematodes. A combination of long-read DNA sequencing technology and bioinformatics will allow us to map the current distribution and identify microbial antagonists that are associated with these pathogens.

Your work will contribute to a better understanding of range-expanding nematode species and the natural suppressive capacity of the associated soils. Together with researchers across Europe, you will help to generate knowledge that can support more resilient soils and sustainable agriculture.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

You will combine advanced molecular techniques, bioinformatics and scientific interpretation. Your main responsibilities are:

analyzing root-knot nematode communities using long-read DNA sequencing technology;
analyzing associated microbial assemblages using long-read DNA sequencing technology;
bioinformatics-based analyses of nematode and microbial communities;
reporting on results to workpackage leads;
communication with European project partners about results and interpretation thereof;
reporting on results to workpackage leads.

Your team

You will work with Hans Helder and Aska Goverse - the Nem-Emerge project coordinators -, as well as with two PhDs that are currently employed on the project. Together, you will exchange knowledge, interpret findings and contribute to the project's scientific objectives.

You will work here

The full title of the EU Horizon Europe project Nem-Emerge is ‘An integrated set of novel approaches to counter the emergence and proliferation of invasive and virulent soil-borne nematodes’. In this position you will contribute to (a) identifying the current distribution of “tropical” root-knot nematode (RKN) species, as well as (b) mapping the endogenous RKN-suppressive capacity of soils.

Your qualities

You have experience in the DNA-based characterization of (soil) microbiomes, preferably using long-read DNA sequencing technologies, as well as with the associated bioinformatics tools

You Also Possess

qualification: MSc in biology, plant sciences, soil sciences or related;
preferably hands-on experience in (soil) microbiome characterization;
hands-on bioinformatics skills (relevant R-packages);
demonstrable (international) project communication skills.

In our international working environment, there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about minimally B2 level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale).

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our collective labour agreement include:

sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. Depending on your experience, we offer a gross salary of between € 3,537.- and € 4,673.- for a full-time working week of 38 hours, in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (https://www.universiteitenvannederland.nl/en/collective-labour-agreement-of-dutch-universities) (scale 8). Additionally, a contract for 0,8 FTE can be discussed. We offer you a temporary contract for the duration of one year.

If you are an internal employee, your current contract is the starting point. Ask your HR Business Partner about your situation specifically. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy (https://wur.service-now.com/esc?id=kb_article&sysparm_article=KB0012172) sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

Coming from abroad

WUR welcomes applications from international candidates. However, for applicants for this specific position from outside the EU/EFTA zone, immigration restrictions may apply based on Dutch and EU immigration laws. Such candidates may be eligible for an “ orientation year ” in the Netherlands or a visa as a “ knowledge migrant ”.

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. If you come with a partner, we offer a Dual Career group program organized by our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/). This program helps your partner to get familiar with the Dutch culture, labour market and assists your partner to find a job.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/expats-new-international-staff) page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.

Important information

For more information about the position, please contact Hans Helder, Associate Professor Laboratory of Nematology, via phone number: +31 17-483136 or via email: hans.helder@wur.nl (mailto:hans.helder@wur.nl).

Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Dax Teunissen, Corporate Recruiter, via email: vacaturemeldingen.psg@wur.nl (mailto:vacaturemeldingen.psg@wur.nl).

Ready to apply?

Click on the application button next to the vacancy on our website. Only applications submitted through our website will be considered.

You can apply up to and including Monday 21 December 2026
. Internal candidates are preferred to apply before 27 November 2026.

Applications are reviewed regularly. Therefore, the position may be filled before the stated closing date.

Welcome, safe, and valued

Wageningen University & Research (WUR) highly values diversity and inclusion because we believe that different insights lead to innovative solutions. We create a work environment where everyone feels welcome, safe, and appreciated, regardless of background, identity, or experience. Together, we are building a culture where everyone's unique contribution adds to the success of our organization.

With its roughly 30 branches, 7,600 employees (6,700 fte) and 13,100 students and over 150,000 participants to WUR’s Life Long Learning, Wageningen University & Research is one of the leading organisations in its domain. new_jobs.title: Research & Development (R&D) Specialist Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Overview

University Hospital Southampton is delighted to offer a fantastic opportunity to work with us

Job Title: Research & Development (R&D) Specialist Data Analyst

Contract Type: Permanent

Please be advised that this vacancy may close earlier than stated if we receive a large number of applications.

Main duties of the job

This is an exciting opportunity to join our growing Data & AI team within the Research & Development department at University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, as a Senior Research Analyst.

Working within the Southampton Emerging Therapies and Technologies (SETT) Centre, you will combine advanced analytical and data engineering expertise with line management responsibilities, leading a group of analysts and data engineers to deliver high-quality research data projects.

Our team supports clinical and academic research through the extraction, processing and analysis of routinely collected healthcare data, developing innovative tools and infrastructure to expand research capacity and improve patient outcomes.

You will play an important role in supporting research project delivery, ensuring technical quality, and working in the team to improve team processes and capabilities.

The SETT Data & AI team works to drive future transformation in patient care through the streamlined extraction of high quality data at scale, and the application of state of the art analytical techniques to drive research. By developing a data landscape friendly to research, we aim to expand Trust-wide research capacity and improve patient outcomes through helping to shape the future of medicine. This is a creative and rapidly evolving unit within the hospital’s R&D environment, and successful candidates will have the exciting opportunity to help shape its direction and long-term aims.

Working for our organisation

As one of the largest acute teaching Trusts in England, we offer learning and development opportunities to help you achieve the career you aspire to. UHS is rated ‘Good’ by the CQC and in the latest national NHS Staff Survey, we were in the top 10 acute trusts for staff engagement and for staff recommending the hospital as a place to work or receive care.

We support flexible working and will consider requests taking into account the needs of the service. UHS employees are able to access a range of NHS discounts, are entitled to a minimum of 35 days paid holiday (pro rata), and we offer a generous pension scheme.

Southampton is an attractive place to live and work situated on the south coast, with an international airport and direct trains to London. The New Forest National Park and beaches of the Jurassic coast are also right on our doorstep. The city offers living costs 30% lower than London and 17 schools rated outstanding by Ofsted.

We believe that using technology wisely shows strong time management and commitment to innovation. However, personalising your recruitment application to highlight your unique skills and experiences is crucial. Relying too heavily on generic, AI-generated content instead of drawing from your own strengths and accomplishments may lead to your application being rejected if multiple candidates present identical or similar information.

Detailed Job Description And Main Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting the delivery of complex research data analysis projects within the Data & AI team. You will support project development and delivery, maintain high technical standards, and contribute to the ongoing improvement of the team's capabilities and working practices.

The Data & AI team works closely with clinical and academic researchers across University Hospital Southampton and partner organisations, supporting a diverse portfolio of research projects using routinely collected healthcare data. Our work ranges from developing automated data extraction and transformation pipelines to undertaking advanced analytical studies, building innovative research tools and improving the infrastructure that enables research at scale. Through this work, we aim to expand research capacity, support scientific discovery and ultimately improve patient outcomes.

Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

Research project development and delivery: Develop and manage a pipeline of research data projects, guiding enquiries from initial Expression of Interest through feasibility assessment, scoping, resource estimation and prioritisation into active delivery. Support the analytical delivery of allocated projects, monitoring progress, and working closely with researchers and research delivery teams to ensure projects meet their scientific and technical requirements.
Technical and analytical leadership: Undertake complex analyses of routinely collected NHS healthcare data, alongside the design and development of robust, reproducible data extraction, transformation and processing pipelines across clinical information systems. Provide technical oversight, including code review, testing, validation and documentation, while supporting the adoption of consistent technical standards and high-quality development practices.
Infrastructure, governance and service development: Contribute to the design and improvement of research data infrastructure, analytical tooling, development environments and automation capabilities to enable efficient and scalable study delivery. Help develop and embed team processes, policies and technical standards through knowledge-sharing, ensuring appropriate information governance and research compliance.

What We’re Looking For

We are looking for a motivated and experienced analyst with an interest in advancing healthcare research.

The following skills and experience would position you well for this role:

Advanced analytical and engineering expertise: Educated to degree level in a numerate or scientific discipline, alongside substantial professional experience in data analysis or data engineering with strong SQL and Python skills, experience working with complex datasets, and a sound understanding of reproducible data processing, software development and quality assurance.
Project delivery and client-facing experience: Demonstrable experience of coordinating and delivering complex analytical or engineering projects in a client-facing environment, with the ability to engage effectively with stakeholders, understand requirements, assess feasibility, agree deliverables, manage expectations and communicate progress, supported by strong interpersonal, communication and relationship-management skills.
Technical judgement and continuous improvement: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, experience of handling sensitive information, an understanding of data protection and quality assurance requirements, and the ability to independently resolve technical challenges, improve working practices and support colleagues through knowledge-sharing and mentoring.

Person specification

Qualifications

Essential criteria

Educated to degree level or able to demonstrate equivalent level of knowledge/research experience relevant to the role.

Knowledge and Experience

Essential criteria

Significant experience of working with SQL to directly interrogate organisational data
Experienced use of Python programming in a working environment for engineering, data science or research
Experience of working with complex data across multiple disparate databases and multi-user environments, being able to demonstrate knowledge of these databases/ software.
Experience of medical research methodology and statutory clinical trial regulations, GCP and research governance requirements.
Experience of clinical trials in the NHS or the commercial health research sector.
Evidence of continuing professional development.
Evidence of ongoing/current Good Clinical Practice Training (GCP)
Thorough understanding of the systems and processes which are used to support the delivery of high quality clinical care in a research environment.
An understanding of R&D issues in the NHS.
Knowledge of research governance and quality assurance systems to ensure safe systems for patients.
Experience of previous training in monitoring of clinical research studies.
Knowledge of data governance requirements including GDPR

Desirable criteria

Commercial research experience.
Previous experience in using IRAS for R&D applications
Experience of working with additional programming languages
Experience of applying machine learning/LLMs within data engineering pipelines
Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, or CI/CD development
Ability to work in multi-disciplinary teams, working with technical and non-technical persons
Experience of working collaboratively with version control tools such as Git

Trust Values

Essential criteria

Patients First
Always Improving
Working Together

new_jobs.title: Biomedical Support Worker
new_jobs.description:
Job Overview

University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust is delighted to offer a fantastic opportunity to work with us.

Job Title: Biomedical Support Worker

Contract Type: Permanent

Hours: 7.5 hours per week - Mondays and Saturdays on a rota basis

UHS will not be able to provide visa Sponsorship
for this vacancy
. Applicants should therefore ensure that they have sufficient right to work in the UK without requiring sponsorship for this role.

Please be advised that this vacancy may close earlier than stated if we receive a large number of applications.

Main duties of the job

We have an exciting opportunity for a band 2 Biomedical Support Worker to work in our Blood Transfusion Laboratory at UHS.

We are looking for a motivated individual to join our BSW team to support our Blood Transfusion Laboratory service. We offer full training and development into the role and opportunities for further development.

The post holder will be expected to undertake a variety of tasks including the delivery of blood and blood products throughout the hospital, stock management and local maintenance of storage equipment.

Please note that this role is for 7.5 hours so you would be expected to work a combination of Mondays and Saturdays only.

Working for our organisation

University Hospital Southampton is one of England's largest acute teaching Trusts, offering a wide range of learning and development opportunities to support your career aspirations.

Located on the south coast with an international airport and direct rail links to London, Southampton offers an ideal setting to live and work, with the New Forest, South Downs and Jurassic Coast.

We believe that using technology wisely shows strong time management and commitment to innovation. However, personalizing your recruitment application to highlight your unique skills and experiences is crucial. Relying too heavily on generic, AI-generated content instead of drawing from your own strengths and accomplishments may lead to your application being rejected if multiple candidates present identical or similar information.

At UHS we’re committed to providing a flexible working environment where possible. Whether you are balancing family, study, or your wellbeing with your career, we want to support you so you can help our patients.

At UHS, we proudly champion individuality, recognizing that outstanding care is only possible with a diverse, inclusive team. We’re committed to creating an anti-racist, anti-discriminatory environment where everyone feels valued, safe, and empowered to make a meaningful impact in our communities. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences to join us in building a healthcare community where everyone can belong, thrive, and contribute.

Detailed Job Description And Main Responsibilities

In this role, your key responsibilities will include:

To receive blood components and products into the laboratory ensuring the cold chain has

remained intact and escalating any issues to the registered healthcare scientist.

To enter blood components and products into stock using the Laboratory Information System

(LIMs).

To pack and transport blood and blood products from the blood transfusion laboratory to clinical

areas and satellite blood fridges using the electronic blood management system.

To prioritise delivery of components to clinical areas based on urgency.
To periodically visit all the satellite blood banks on the SGH and PAH sites and return all unused

blood to the laboratory.

To maintain all UHS blood component storage facilities including cleaning and checking local and

remote alarm systems.

To collect blood and blood products from NHSBT including urgent ad hoc collections.
To escalate alarms and warnings generated by the electronic blood management system to a

registered healthcare scientist.

To complete daily data submissions for blood component stock and wastage to NHSBT via the

Vanessa platform.

Using templates from Charts issue letters to patients offering feotal RhD screening.
To complete weekly stock checks and escalate any deficiencies in stock to the advanced

Biomedical Scientists.

To receive deliveries into the department and complete the required documentation following

laboratory SOPs.

To carry out basic audits as directed by the Transfusion Laboratory Manager.
Demonstrate own working practices to new members of staff.
To maintain a personal training record to demonstrate competence and compliance with statutory

and mandatory training.

Person specification

Qualifications, Knowledge And Experience

Essential criteria

GCSE level 4+ or equivalent in at least two from Maths, English and Science

Desirable criteria

Previous experience in a medical laboratory
IT competency (Microsoft, Outlook, hospital IT systems)

new_jobs.title: Research Associate in Pure Mathematics
new_jobs.description:
Applications are invited for the above post, to start in April 2027 for a fixed term of six months.

The successful applicant will work with Prof Gareth Jones and Dr Martin Orr on the EPSRC-funded project “Effective methods in o-minimality and diophantine geometry”. The project aims to combine ideas from o-minimality with tools from diophantine geometry to make progress on unlikely intersection problems. Depending on the background of the person appointed, they may carry out research related more closely to o-minimality or to diophantine geometry, or both.

Applications should normally be made online. Candidates should provide a full academic CV, to which they should append a brief research statement outlining their research record and future plans (maximum 2 pages).

You will be responsible for:

Conducting individual and collaborative research projects
Writing up research work for publication
Contributing to the research life of the Department of Mathematics by participating in and organising research events and activities

We welcome candidates who bring diverse perspectives, experiences, and approaches to their work.

About You

We encourage applications from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. You should demonstrate:

Essential Criteria

Has, or expects shortly to obtain, a PhD or equivalent research experience in mathematics or a closely related discipline;
a strong record of original research in an area of number theory or model theory relevant to the project, commensurate with career stage;
strong research potential evidenced by a personal research plan;
strong communication skills in written and spoken English.

Desirable criteria

research experience in o-minimality or diophantine geometry.

Interviews will take place during the week beginning 4 January 2027

is seeking a skilled Analytical Biochemist and/or Biologist
at the Research Associate level to join a team focused on supporting gene therapy & enzyme replacement therapy.
